claim: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is the most prevalent histologic tumor subtype of ovarian carcinoma.
source: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most prevalent histologic tumor subtype (Matulonis et al., 2016), is treated with a combination of cytoreductive surgery and carboplatin (DNA damage generation) and paclitaxel (microtubule-stabilizing drug) chemotherapy.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Matulonis et al., 2016.

claim: HGSOC is treated with a combination of cytoreductive surgery and carboplatin and paclitaxel chemotherapy.
source: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most prevalent histologic tumor subtype (Matulonis et al., 2016), is treated with a combination of cytoreductive surgery and carboplatin (DNA damage generation) and paclitaxel (microtubule-stabilizing drug) chemotherapy.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Matulonis et al., 2016.

claim: Approximately 80% of patients with HGSOC exhibit serial disease recurrence, develop resistance to platinum chemotherapy, and die.
source: Approximately 80% of patients with HGSOC exhibit serial disease recurrence, develop resistance to platinum chemotherapy, and die (Bowtell et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bowtell et al., 2015.

claim: Gains at 8q24 occur in most HGSOC tumors and encompass the MYC oncogene at 8q24.21.
source: Gains at 8q24 occur in most HGSOC tumors and encompass the MYC oncogene at 8q24.21 (Gorringe et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gorringe et al., 2010.

claim: The PTK2 gene at 8q24.3, encoding focal adhesion kinase (FAK), is frequently amplified in breast, uterine, cervical, and ovarian tumors.
source: The PTK2 gene at 8q24.3, encoding focal adhesion kinase (FAK), is frequently amplified in breast, uterine, cervical, and ovarian tumors (Kaveh et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kaveh et al., 2016.

claim: HGSOC tumors with PTK2 gains exhibit elevated FAK expression and FAK Y397 phosphorylation.
source: HGSOC tumors with PTK2 gains exhibit elevated FAK expression and FAK Y397 phosphorylation (Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2011; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2011 and Zhang et al., 2016.

claim: ID8-IP cells (KMF cells) were isolated via early recovery of ascites-associated cells and anchorage-independent expansion ex vivo.
source: We previously isolated aggressive ID8-IP cells, lethal in mice within 40 days (Ward et al., 2013), via early recovery of ascites-associated cells and anchorage-independent expansion ex vivo (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ward et al., 2013 and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Total exome sequencing of ID8 and ID8-IP cells revealed 19619 shared, 29373 ID8 unique, and 11800 ID8-IP unique gene variants.
source: Total exome sequencing (90% of exons sequenced at 100X) of ID8 and ID8-IP cells revealed 19619 shared, 29373 ID8 unique, and 11800 ID8-IP unique gene variants.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from exome sequencing.

claim: The mutational burden within both ID8 and ID8-IP cells is low.
source: Overall, the mutational burden within both ID8 and ID8-IP cells is low.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the exome sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: ID8-IP cells contain gains in murine chromosome cytoband regions 6qD1-G3, 15qD3-F3, and 15qA1-D3.
source: Gains in murine chromosome cytoband regions 6qD1-G3, 15qD3-F3, and 15qA1-D3 were present in ID8-IP cells (Figure 1B, green circles).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from exome sequencing and bioinformatic analyses shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Murine chromosome cytoband regions 6qD1-G3, 15qD3-F3, and 15qA1-D3 in ID8-IP cells correspond to human cytobands 12p12.1, 8q24.2, and 8q24.3.
source: These correspond to human cytobands 12p12.1, 8q24.2, and 8q24.3.
evidence: The claim is based on bioinformatic mapping of murine to human cytobands.

claim: Common gene gains in ID8-IP and HGSOC include Kras, Myc, and Ptk2 (encoding FAK).
source: Notably, common gene gains in ID8-IP and HGSOC include Kras, Myc, and Ptk2 (encoding FAK) that support proliferation, stem cells, and adhesion signaling, respectively (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Table 1.

claim: In HGSOC patients, simultaneous gains in KRAS, MYC, and PTK2 co-occur in 42% of tumors.
source: In HGSOC patients, simultaneous gains in KRAS, MYC, and PTK2 gains co-occur in 42% of tumors; PTK2 and MYC co-occur in an additional 32% of HGSOC patients (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: More than 70% of HGSOC tumors contain combined gains at PTK2 and MYC loci.
source: Thus, more than 70% of HGSOC tumors contain combined gains at PTK2 and MYC loci.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing 42% with KRAS, MYC, and PTK2 gains and 32% with PTK2 and MYC gains.

claim: PTK2 copy number gains are linearly proportional to PTK2 mRNA (R2 = 0.66) and FAK protein (R2 = 0.61) levels in HGSOC tumors.
source: PTK2 copy number gains are linearly proportional to PTK2 mRNA (R2 = 0.66) and FAK protein (R2 = 0.61) levels in HGSOC tumors (Figure 1C—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Elevated PTK2 mRNA levels in HGSOC are associated with decreased patient relapse-free survival (n = 1435, p=0.0009, and hazard ratio = 1.25).
source: Elevated PTK2 mRNA levels in HGSOC are associated with decreased patient relapse-free survival (n = 1435, p=0.0009, and hazard ratio = 1.25) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A 36 gene set associated with PTK2 gain was associated with a significant shorter time to relapse (n = 575, p=0.0024, hazard ratio = 1.37).
source: This 36 gene set was associated with a significant shorter time to relapse (n = 575, p=0.0024, hazard ratio = 1.37) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: KMF cells exhibit a mesenchymal morphology, form foci in two-dimensional (2D) cell culture, and readily form 3D colonies in methylcellulose.
source: KMF cells exhibit a mesenchymal morphology, form foci in two-dimensional (2D) cell culture, and readily form 3D colonies in methylcellulose (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: KMF tumorspheres expressed elevated FAK, increased FAK Y397 phosphorylation, and decreased E-cadherin and β-catenin protein levels relative to ID8 cells.
source: By immunoblotting, KMF tumorspheres expressed elevated FAK, increased FAK Y397 phosphorylation, and decreased E-cadherin and β-catenin protein levels relative to ID8 cells and normalized to actin (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Treatment of KMF tumorspheres with a glycogen synthase kinase-3 inhibitor (GSK3i) increased β-catenin protein and nuclear transcriptional activity.
source: Treatment of KMF tumorspheres with a glycogen synthase kinase-3 inhibitor (GSK3i) increased β-catenin protein and nuclear transcriptional activity whereas GSK3i addition had no effects on β-catenin levels or activity in ID8 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Greater than 10% of KMF tumorspheres possessed high ALDH activity with less than 1% of ID8 cells being ALDH-positive.
source: Additionally, greater than 10% of KMF tumorspheres possessed high ALDH activity with less than 1% of ID8 cells being ALDH-positive (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ALDEFLUOR assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: RNA sequencing identified 10800 shared, 744 ID8 enriched, and 402 KMF elevated transcripts.
source: Using FPKM (Fragments Per Kilobase of transcript per Million mapped reads) threshold values greater than one, 10800 shared, 744 ID8 enriched, and 402 KMF elevated transcripts were identified (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Top 20 Reactome signaling pathways upregulated in KMF cells include Cell Cycle Control, Mitotic Checkpoint, DNA Repair, and Rho GTPase signaling.
source: Top 20 Reactome signaling pathways upregulated in KMF cells include Cell Cycle Control, Mitotic Checkpoint, DNA Repair, and Rho GTPase signaling (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Reactome pathway analysis data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: KMF cells possessed increased intrinsic resistance to CP cytotoxicity with greater than a 10-fold difference in EC50 values compared to ID8.
source: KMF cells possessed increased intrinsic resistance to CP cytotoxicity with greater than a 10-fold difference in EC50 values compared to ID8.
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data.

claim: FAK pY397 staining remained elevated in non-necrotic tumor samples obtained after multiple cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
source: Surprisingly, pY397 FAK staining remained elevated in non-necrotic tumor samples obtained after multiple cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: pY397 FAK levels trended significantly upward in tumors surviving neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
source: By comparing samples from the same patients pre- and post-chemotherapy, we found pY397 FAK levels trended significantly upward in tumors surviving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (Figure 3D), further supporting an association between FAK signaling and tumor chemoresistance.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: FAK Y397 phosphorylation was restored as OVCAR3 cells clustered to form tumorspheres within 2–3 days.
source: However, extended time course analyses of OVCAR3 cells cultured in anchorage-independent PromoCell media revealed that FAK Y397 phosphorylation was restored as OVCAR3 cells clustered to form tumorspheres within 2–3 days (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: CP (1 µM) treatment of OVCAR3 tumorspheres triggered increased FAK Y397 and β-catenin Y142 phosphorylation.
source: Surprisingly, CP (1 µM) treatment of OVCAR3 tumorspheres (EC50 >10 µM) triggered increased FAK Y397 and β-catenin Y142 phosphorylation (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CP treatment resulted in increased tumorsphere formation and ALDEFLUOR activity in OVCAR3 and KMF cells.
source: CP treatment resulted in increased tumorsphere formation and ALDEFLUOR activity in OVCAR3 and KMF cells, consistent with this low CP dose serving as an activation-type stress (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: FAK inhibitor (FAKi) reduced tumorsphere formation and ALDEFLUOR activity compared to control-treated OVCAR3 and KMF cells.
source: In contrast, FAK inhibitor (FAKi) reduced tumorsphere formation and ALDEFLUOR activity compared to control-treated OVCAR3 and KMF cells (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Only CP combined with FAKi decreased tumorsphere viability.
source: FAKi was not directly cytotoxic, since only CP combined with FAKi decreased tumorsphere viability (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: CP-resistant A2780-CP70 and OVCAR10-CP cells exhibited a newly acquired dose-dependent sensitivity to FAKi growth inhibition as tumorspheres.
source: In addition, we find that CP-resistant A2780-CP70 and OVCAR10-CP cells exhibited a newly acquired dose-dependent sensitivity to FAKi growth inhibition as tumorspheres (Figure 6B), but not when the same cells were grown in 2D conditions (Figure 6B—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth assay data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6B—figure supplement 1.

claim: FAKi selectively prevented A2780-CP70 and OVCAR10-CP methylcellulose colony formation.
source: FAKi selectively prevented A2780-CP70 and OVCAR10-CP methylcellulose colony formation (Figure 6F) but did not inhibit parental A2780 or OVCAR10 colony formation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: FAKi with CP prevented OVCAR10-CP colony formation and this was associated with increased OVCAR10-CP apoptosis.
source: FAKi with CP prevented colony formation (Figure 6H) and this was associated with increased OVCAR10-CP apoptosis (Figure 6I).
evidence: The claim is supported by colony formation and apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 6H,I.

claim: Single-agent FAKi treatment reduced A2780-CP70 tumor mass approximately 40% compared to controls.
source: In dramatic contrast, in A2780-CP70 tumors, single-agent FAKi treatment reduced tumor mass approximately 40% compared to controls (Figure 7A,D), and the combination of FAKi with CPT chemotherapy resulted in an even greater reduction in tumor growth (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 7A,D.

claim: The combination of FAKi with CPT chemotherapy resulted in an even greater reduction in A2780-CP70 tumor growth.
source: In dramatic contrast, in A2780-CP70 tumors, single-agent FAKi treatment reduced tumor mass approximately 40% compared to controls (Figure 7A,D), and the combination of FAKi with CPT chemotherapy resulted in an even greater reduction in tumor growth (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 7B–D.

claim: CPT treatment increased FAK Y397 phosphorylation and ALDH-1A1 staining in non-necrotic regions of A2780-CP70 tumors.
source: Interestingly, CPT treatment increased FAK Y397 phosphorylation (Figure 7E,F) and ALDH-1A1 staining (Figure 7G) in non-necrotic regions of A2780-CP70 tumors (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7E,F,G and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Adding FAKi to CPT chemotherapy suppressed FAK Y397 phosphorylation, reduced ALDH-1A1 tumor staining, and increased tumor apoptosis in vivo.
source: Adding FAKi to CPT chemotherapy suppressed FAK Y397 phosphorylation, reduced ALDH-1A1 tumor staining, and increased tumor apoptosis in vivo (Figure 7E,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, and TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 7E,H.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 targeting was used to inactivate murine Ptk2 exon four in KMF cells to create FAK knockout (KO) cells.
source: To provide genetic support for the role of FAK in intrinsic CP resistance, CRISPR/Cas9 targeting was used to inactivate murine Ptk2 exon four in KMF cells (Figure 8) and human PTK2 exon 3 of OVCAR3 cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) to create FAK knockout (KO) cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the CRISPR/Cas9 method and reference to Figure 8.

claim: Exome sequencing of FAK KO clone KT13 detected only 165 unique variants, including the four Ptk2 alterations, indicating that CRISPR targeting was specific.
source: Exome sequencing of FAK KO clone KT13 (90% of exons sequenced at 100X) detected only 165 unique variants, including the four Ptk2 alterations, indicating that CRISPR targeting was specific and that the FAK KO KT13 genome is similar to parental KMF cells (Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by exome sequencing data.

claim: FAK KO cells exhibited sensitivity to CP-mediated cytotoxicity compared to parental KMF cells.
source: However, FAK KO cells exhibited sensitivity to CP-mediated cytotoxicity compared to parental KMF cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data.

claim: Phenotypes of decreased tumorsphere formation, ALDEFLUOR activity, and CP resistance in FAK KO OVCAR3 cells were rescued by GFP-FAK re-expression.
source: Importantly, phenotypes of decreased tumorsphere formation, ALDEFLUOR activity, and CP resistance in FAK KO OVCAR3 cells were rescued by GFP-FAK re-expression (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: In 3D anchorage-independent conditions, GFP-FAK-WT and GFP-FAK-R454 were equally expressed, but only GFP-FAK-WT was phosphorylated at Y397.
source: In 3D anchorage-independent conditions, GFP-FAK-WT and GFP-FAK-R454 were equally expressed, but only GFP-FAK-WT was phosphorylated at Y397 (Figure 8D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Elevated levels of extracellular matrix (collagen type six and laminin), surface receptors (N-cadherin and Nectin-2), β-catenin, and Wnt signaling targets (GPC4) were present in FAK-WT compared to FAK KO cells.
source: Elevated levels of extracellular matrix (collagen type six and laminin), surface receptors (N-cadherin and Nectin-2), β-catenin, and Wnt signaling targets (GPC4) (Sakane et al., 2012) were present in FAK-WT compared to FAK KO cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and a citation to Sakane et al., 2012.

claim: FAK-WT restored total ALDEFLUOR activity, ALDH-1A2, ALDH-1B1, and Myc protein levels in FAK KO cells equivalent to parental KMF cells.
source: FAK-WT restored total ALDEFLUOR activity, ALDH-1A2, ALDH-1B1, and Myc protein levels in FAK KO cells equivalent to parental KMF cells (Figure 9A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ALDEFLUOR assay and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 9A,C.

claim: Expression of FAK-WT and β-catenin ΔGSK but not FAK-R454 significantly enhanced FAK KO resistance to CP cytotoxicity in vitro.
source: Expression of FAK-WT and β-catenin ΔGSK but not FAK-R454 significantly enhanced FAK KO resistance to CP cytotoxicity in vitro (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Intrinsic FAK activity is essential for KMF tumor establishment in mice.
source: Importantly, these results reveal that intrinsic FAK activity is essential for KMF tumor establishment in mice.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the in vivo tumor growth experiments showing FAK KO and FAK-R454 cells did not grow as tumors.

claim: β-catenin signaling was not sufficient to support KMF tumor growth in the absence of FAK.
source: Moreover, β-catenin signaling was not sufficient to support KMF tumor growth in the absence of FAK.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo tumor growth data showing β-catenin ΔGSK did not promote FAK KO tumor growth.

claim: 1040 mRNA transcripts were increased two-fold or more by FAK compared to FAK KO cells.
source: Using an FPKM cutoff greater than one, 1040 mRNA transcripts were increased two-fold or more by FAK compared to FAK KO cells and significant after multiple testing correction (Figure 10—source data 1 ).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing data.

claim: 591 genes were identified as FAK activity-dependent and showed KEGG pathway enrichment for MAPK Signaling, Cell Cycle, Axon Guidance, and DNA Replication.
source: By filtering out transcripts that were elevated in FAK-R454 versus FAK KO cells (FAK activity-independent targets), 591 genes were identified as FAK activity-dependent and showed KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes) pathway enrichment for MAPK Signaling, Cell Cycle, Axon Guidance, and DNA Replication.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing and KEGG pathway analysis data.

claim: 241 shared transcripts were identified as co-regulated by FAK activity and β-catenin.
source: After unbiased filtering of the 591 FAK activity-dependent transcripts with those elevated by β-catenin ΔGSK, 241 shared transcripts were identified as co-regulated by FAK activity and β-catenin (Figure 10A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and filtering analysis shown in Figure 10A.

claim: 135 targets matched between the 241 shared FAK and β-catenin murine targets and genes elevated in HGSOC.
source: Last, the 241 shared FAK and β-catenin murine targets were filtered against genes elevated in HGSOC by querying TCGA. Notably, 135 targets matched, 77 exhibit frequent gains in 20% of tumors, and 19 genes were elevated in greater than 50% of HGSOC patient tumors (Figure 10A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and TCGA analysis shown in Figure 10A.

claim: Myc was the most common gene target among the 19 genes elevated in greater than 50% of HGSOC patient tumors.
source: Myc was the most common gene target and immunoblotting of KMF, FAK KO, and FAK-WT lysates confirmed the regulation of Myc protein expression by FAK (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Quantitative PCR verified at least twofold changes in genes linked to DNA repair (Recq4l, Spc24, Pkmyt1, Dscc1, and Rnf144b) or pluripotency (Wnt4, Klf5, Amigo2, Fos, and Ndufa4l2) that were elevated by FAK-WT re-expression.
source: Quantitative PCR using independent experimental samples verified at least twofold changes in genes linked to DNA repair (Recq4l, Spc24, Pkmyt1, Dscc1, and Rnf144b) or pluripotency (Wnt4, Klf5, Amigo2, Fos, and Ndufa4l2) that were elevated by FAK-WT re-expression (Figure 10B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 10B.
